chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Imran ibn Muhammad, who said:

I said to Abi Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, I have an estate at a distance of fifteen miles, five farsakhs. So at times I go out to it and stay there for three days, or five days, or seven days. Should I perform the salat in full or shorten it? He said: Shorten on the road, and perform it in full at the estate.

key_terms.أُتِمُّ: I perform the salat in full, without shortening
key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: I shorten the salat as a traveler
key_terms.أُقِيمُ: I stay or reside for a number of days
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ فَرَاسِخَ: five farsakhs, indicating the travel distance mentioned in the question
key_terms.ضَيْعَةً: an estate or landed property that the person travels to
key_terms.فِي الضَّيْعَةِ: at the estate itself, upon being there
key_terms.فِي الطَّرِيقِ: while on the road or in transit

ai.seo_question: Should a person shorten salat while traveling to his estate and complete it upon arrival?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about salat during travel to one's estate. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between the state of being on the road, where one shortens the salat, and being at the estate itself, where one performs it in full.
